an10.219:1.1: “Bhikkhus, I do not say that there is a termination of volitional kamma that has been done and accumulated so long as one has not experienced its results,
an10.219:1.2: and that may be in this very life, or in the next rebirth, or on some subsequent occasion.
an10.219:1.3: But I do not say that there is making an end of suffering so long as one has not experienced the results of volitional kamma that has been done and accumulated.
an10.219:2.1: “This noble disciple, bhikkhus, who is thus devoid of longing, devoid of ill will, unconfused, clearly comprehending, ever mindful, dwells pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the second quarter, the third quarter, and the fourth quarter. Thus above, below, across, and everywhere, and to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, vast, exalted, measureless, without enmity, without ill will.
an10.219:3.2: ‘Previously, my mind was limited and undeveloped, but now it is measureless and well developed. No measurable kamma remains or persists there.’
an10.219:4.2: if a youth were to develop the liberation of mind by loving-kindness from his childhood on, would he do a bad deed?”
an10.219:5.1: “Could suffering affect him if he does no bad deed?”
an10.219:5.3: For on what account could suffering affect one who does no bad deed?”
an10.219:6.1: “A woman or a man should develop this liberation of mind by loving-kindness.
an10.219:6.2: A woman or a man cannot take this body with them when they go.
an10.219:6.3: Mortals have mind as their core.
an10.219:6.5: ‘Whatever bad deed I did here in the past with this deed-born body is all to be experienced here.
an10.219:6.7: When the liberation of mind by loving-kindness has been developed in this way, it leads to non-returning for a wise bhikkhu here who does not penetrate to a further liberation.
an10.219:7.1: “This noble disciple, bhikkhus, who is thus devoid of longing, devoid of ill will, unconfused, clearly comprehending, ever mindful, dwells pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion …
an10.219:7.2: with a mind imbued with altruistic joy …
an10.219:7.3: with a mind imbued with equanimity, likewise the second quarter, the third quarter, and the fourth quarter.
an10.219:7.4: Thus above, below, across, and everywhere, and to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with equanimity, vast, exalted, measureless, without enmity, without ill will.
an10.219:8.2: ‘Previously, my mind was limited and undeveloped, but now it is measureless and well developed. No measurable kamma remains or persists there.’
an10.219:9.2: if a youth would develop the liberation of mind by equanimity, from his childhood on, would he do a bad deed?”
an10.219:10.1: “Could suffering affect him if he does no bad deed?”
an10.219:10.3: For on what account could suffering affect one who does no bad deed?”
an10.219:11.1: “A woman or a man should develop this liberation of mind by equanimity.
an10.219:11.2: A woman or a man cannot take this body with them when they go.
an10.219:11.3: Mortals have mind as their core.
an10.219:11.5: ‘Whatever bad deed I did here in the past with this deed-born body is all to be experienced here.
an10.219:11.7: When the liberation of mind by equanimity has been developed in this way, it leads to non-returning for a wise bhikkhu here who does not penetrate to a further liberation.”
